subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main aim of samatha meditation?
options: Worshipping the Buddha as a god
questions.explain: Samatha meditation aims to calm and concentrate the mind, often through focusing on the breath.

questions.q: Which two major traditions of Buddhism are commonly contrasted?
questions.explain: Theravada and Mahayana are the two main branches of Buddhism.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Three Marks of Existence?
questions.explain: Anicca, meaning impermanence, is one of the Three Marks of Existence alongside anatta and dukkha.

questions.q: What was the birth name of the Buddha?
questions.explain: The Buddha was born Siddhartha Gautama, a prince in what is now Nepal.

questions.q: What does 'nibbana' (nirvana) refer to?
options: The blowing out of craving and the end of suffering
A heaven ruled by a god
questions.explain: Nibbana is the 'blowing out' of craving, ending suffering and the cycle of rebirth.

questions.q: The 'Four Sights' that Siddhartha saw included an old man, a sick man, a dead man and:
questions.explain: The fourth sight was a holy man, which inspired Siddhartha to seek the cause of suffering.

questions.q: What is 'samsara' in Buddhist teaching?
options: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
questions.explain: Samsara is the continuous cycle of birth, death and rebirth driven by karma.

questions.q: Vipassana meditation is mainly concerned with developing:
options: Insight into the true nature of reality
questions.explain: Vipassana meditation develops insight into the true nature of reality, such as impermanence.

questions.q: In the Theravada tradition, the ideal figure to aspire to is the:
options: Bodhisattva who delays nirvana to help others
questions.explain: In Theravada Buddhism the ideal is the arhat, one who achieves enlightenment and escapes rebirth.

questions.q: Where did Siddhartha attain enlightenment?
questions.explain: Siddhartha attained enlightenment while meditating beneath the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.

questions.q: Before reaching enlightenment, Siddhartha first tried which approach to find the truth?
options: A life of severe self-denial and extreme asceticism
Worshipping many gods at a temple
questions.explain: Siddhartha first practised extreme asceticism but found it did not lead to truth, so he chose the Middle Way.

questions.q: How many factors make up the Buddhist Eightfold Path?
questions.explain: The Eightfold Path has eight factors, such as right view, right action and right mindfulness.

questions.q: In Mahayana Buddhism, a bodhisattva is someone who:
options: Rules as a king over a Buddhist land
Delays their own nirvana to help others reach enlightenment
Rejects the teachings of the Buddha
questions.explain: In Mahayana Buddhism a bodhisattva compassionately delays final nirvana to help others reach enlightenment.

questions.q: The Third Noble Truth teaches that:
questions.explain: The Third Noble Truth (nirodha) teaches that suffering can be ended by removing craving.

questions.q: In Buddhism, karma refers to:
options: Intentional actions that shape future experience
questions.explain: Karma is the principle that intentional actions have consequences that shape future experience and rebirth.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Three Refuges (Three Jewels)?
questions.explain: The Three Refuges are the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha (the community of Buddhists).

questions.q: What does the term 'dukkha' refer to?
questions.explain: Dukkha means suffering or unsatisfactoriness and is one of the Three Marks of Existence.

questions.q: The three sections of the Eightfold Path are wisdom, meditation and:
questions.explain: The Eightfold Path is grouped into wisdom, ethics (morality) and meditation.

questions.q: The First Noble Truth states that:
options: The path is the way to end suffering
questions.explain: The First Noble Truth is that life involves suffering (dukkha).

questions.q: What does 'anatta' teach in Buddhism?
options: The world was created by a god
There is no permanent, fixed self
There is an eternal, unchanging soul
questions.explain: Anatta teaches that there is no permanent, fixed self or soul.

questions.q: The Dhamma (Dharma), one of the Three Refuges, refers to:
options: The Buddhist community of monks and nuns
questions.explain: The Dhamma is the teachings of the Buddha, one of the Three Refuges alongside the Buddha and the Sangha.

questions.q: Which of these is a factor of the Eightfold Path?
questions.explain: Right intention is one of the eight factors of the Eightfold Path, the way to end suffering.
